questions.q: A company suffers a distributed denial-of-service attack that renders its portal inaccessible for four hours. Which pillar of the CIA triad is directly impacted?
questions.explain: A DDoS attack prevents access to the service: this impacts availability. Confidentiality and integrity are not necessarily compromised.

questions.q: A user logs in with their password and a TOTP code. Which AAA function comes immediately after this step?
questions.explain: Authentication establishes identity; authorization then determines what that identity can do. Accounting tracks actions.

questions.q: Which elements directly contribute to non-repudiation? (Select all that apply)
options: A digital signature using the sender's private key
A trusted timestamp issued by a third party
A shared password among multiple administrators
questions.explain: Non-repudiation requires third-party verifiable proof: signature, timestamp, and an intact log. A shared password does not prove who acted.

questions.q: An administrator has standing administrative access on all servers 'to work faster.' Which principle is violated?
questions.explain: Least privilege requires the minimum access necessary for the required duration. Standing, global access exceeds the need.

questions.q: In a development pipeline, the same person writes the code, approves it, and deploys it to production. Which principle is primarily violated?
questions.explain: Separation of duties prevents a single person from executing a critical action end-to-end. Here, no independent review is possible.

questions.q: Which statement best describes defense in depth?
options: Installing multiple antivirus products on each workstation
Layering independent controls across diverse layers
questions.explain: Depth comes from the diversity of layers, not the number of products. Multiple antivirus tools cover the same failure mode.

questions.q: Which statement corresponds to the Zero Trust model?
options: The internal network is trusted; the external network is not
No zone is trusted by default; every access is verified based on context
All users must use a VPN
A firewall is sufficient if its policy is strict
questions.explain: Zero Trust removes implicit trust, including inside the network. Verification is contextual and continuous.

questions.q: A visible surveillance camera at a building entrance is primarily what type of control?
questions.explain: When visible, it deters through the fear of being observed. If footage is analyzed after the fact, it becomes detective. The prompt specifies a visible camera: deterrent.

questions.q: An IPS blocks malicious traffic in real time. How should it be classified?
questions.explain: An IPS blocks the traffic: preventive. An IDS, which alerts without blocking, is detective.

questions.q: A password policy defines minimum length and complexity, but no technology enforces it. What type of control is this?
questions.explain: The policy is managerial (category) and directive (it guides behavior). It does not technically prevent non-compliance.

questions.q: A critical server cannot be patched. The team adds a WAF and enhanced monitoring. Which control type best describes this response?
questions.explain: The control compensates for an unpatchable vulnerability. The WAF may block (preventive in mechanism), but its role here is compensating.

questions.q: Match each control to its primary category.
questions.explain: The category describes the nature of the control, not its timing. Log review is a day-to-day operations activity: operational.

questions.q: Which control is both corrective and operational?
options: A daily tested and restorable backup
questions.explain: Backups restore systems after an incident (corrective) and are part of routine operations (operational).

questions.q: Which of the following are Zero Trust principles? (Select all that apply)
options: Assume the internal network is safe
questions.explain: Zero Trust explicitly verifies, applies least privilege, assumes breach, and segments by application. Assuming the internal network is safe is the opposite of the model.

questions.q: An audit log is stored on the server it monitors, accessible by a local administrator account. What is the main flaw?
options: An attacker who compromises the server can modify or delete the log
The log consumes too much disk space
questions.explain: Accounting is only reliable if an attacker cannot alter the trail. Logs must be centralized and integrity-protected.
